title: Meeting Minutes Workbench
summary: A Cantonese transcript goes in; minutes in the department's exact Word format come out. Two language-model passes, one script, and no instructions needed from the user.

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: The minutes format is strict and old: numbered sections, set fonts, a table nobody wants to rebuild. Pasting a transcript into a chatbot gives text that never matches it, so the secretary spends the afternoon reformatting.

sections.heading: Two passes on purpose
paragraphs: The first pass understands: it fixes transcription errors, cuts the meeting into the template's seven sections and marks anything it could not hear. The second writes: formal Chinese, official tone, no number touched. A script then pours the result into the Word template.
sections.quote: Missing content → fix pass one. Wrong tone → fix pass two. Never start over.

sections.heading: The output is the template itself
paragraphs: Not "like" the template — the same file with the text swapped and the formatting untouched. Unclear lines are flagged in place instead of guessed; date, time and venue are left for the secretary.
